senses.definition: A microphone that uses a moving coil of wire or thin metal ribbon near a magnet to turn sound into an electrical signal.
senses.example: We spoke into a dynamic microphone to record the announcement.

senses.definition: A wide moving part inside many speakers that pushes on the air to make sound.
senses.example: The speaker cone moved in and out as the music played.

senses.definition: A two-pronged metal tool that vibrates at a steady rate to give a reference note.
senses.example: The teacher tapped a tuning fork before the choir began.

senses.definition: Reducing a sound by making waves that partly cancel its pressure changes.
senses.example: The headphones used noise cancellation to make the motor hum harder to hear.

senses.definition: A musical instrument with keys that control the flow of air into pipes of different sizes.
senses.example: The player pressed three pipe organ keys and heard three notes together.

senses.definition: Concrete with other material inside, often steel rods, that helps it hold together under a load.
senses.example: Reinforced concrete helped the bridge deck carry passing buses.

senses.definition: A way to lay bricks in rows so the end of a brick sits over part of a brick below it instead of above another end.
senses.example: The running bond made a repeating pattern on the school wall.

senses.definition: A wide base under a wall or post that spreads its load over more ground.
senses.example: The column stood on a spread footing wider than the column itself.

senses.definition: A wall that holds back soil so one side can be higher than the other.
senses.example: A retaining wall kept the garden soil above the walking path.

senses.definition: A place between parts that leaves room for them to move as they get bigger or smaller.
senses.example: An expansion joint let the road deck shift a little in warm weather.

senses.definition: A bridge with cables running directly between its towers and points along the roadway or path.
senses.example: The cables of the cable-stayed bridge spread out like fans.

senses.definition: A window with two sheets of glass and a sealed space between them.
senses.example: A double-pane window helped slow the movement of heat out of the room.

senses.definition: A channel that catches rain running off an edge of a roof and guides it toward a drain or pipe.
senses.example: The roof gutter caught water that slid down the shingles.

senses.definition: A short slope that joins a sidewalk and a street where there would otherwise be a step.
senses.example: We rolled our wagon down the curb ramp at the corner.

senses.definition: A paved surface with openings that let some water move down through it.
senses.example: Rain sank through the permeable pavement beside the library.

senses.definition: A curved part of a drain that holds water to block air and smells from farther down the pipe.
senses.example: A drain trap under the sink held a small amount of water.

senses.definition: A piece at the end of a faucet that mixes air into the stream of water.
senses.example: The faucet aerator made the running water look bubbly.

senses.definition: A rod that goes through parts of a hinge so they can turn around it together.
senses.example: The door swung around its hinge pins each time we opened it.
